thedotmack/claude-mem ↗ 2 releases · 2 stable
v15.19.0 Stable2026-11-16T02:04:44Z

Continue a Claude Code or Codex conversation from My Work

Open a request in My Work, then open "Where this came from". Under each Claude Code or Codex conversation there is now a message box. Type a message and press Send, and that same conversation takes the turn. The reply shows right there (#6191; the command shapes follow @wiesenthal's answer code in #6054, and the commit credits him).

  • Each conversation keeps the messages you sent from My Work and their replies, in order. Stop ends a running turn.
  • The box says which folder the turn runs in. When the recorded folder no longer exists (common after a worktree is cleaned up), the turn runs in the nearest existing folder above it.
  • "Copy resume command" copies claude --resume <id> or codex resume <id>. On a Mac, "Open in Claude" opens a Claude Code conversation in the Claude desktop app.
  • One Send starts one headless resume (claude --resume <id> -p --output-format json, or codex exec resume <id> - --skip-git-repo-check) with your message on stdin. A failed turn is recorded as failed and never retried. Nothing is queued or saved for replay, and nothing starts at startup, on a timer or on reconnect.
  • A worker restart or shutdown stops every running turn first, so a restarted worker never becomes a second writer on the same conversation. Nothing re-sends a stopped turn.
  • A turn runs in your own default permission mode, the same one claude -p --resume uses in your terminal. In Manual mode, tool calls that need approval are denied and the row counts them. No permission, model or sandbox flag is passed.
  • The new routes answer only on loopback and refuse other origins. With local API token mode off, another program on the same computer can call them, as it can every other worker route. On a shared computer, turn on local API token mode.
  • One change for every request: while a newer version of an open request loads, the drawer keeps showing the version it already has instead of "Loading request detail…".

Known limits:

  • The Codex path through the page was not run end to end on the test machine. Codex turns were checked at the runner level with the real CLI.
  • On Windows, Stop may not reach a CLI behind a .cmd shim, and "Open in Claude" is not offered.
  • A conversation that is mid-turn in a terminal can still get a turn from My Work. Claude Code's docs say two writers on one session can lose messages. My Work blocks two of its own turns on one conversation.
  • A worker crash (not a graceful restart) cannot stop a running turn. It finishes on its own.
  • A helper the CLI leaves behind, such as a slow-exiting MCP server, keeps the turn marked as running until it exits or you press Stop.

Bring your existing memory

npx claude-mem import fetches memories straight from Mem0 Platform or Supermemory and saves them as searchable observations in a project you choose. No export file and no model calls (#6106).

# MEM0_API_KEY in the environment
npx claude-mem import --from mem0 --source-account personal-mem0 --user my-user-id --project imported-memory

# SUPERMEMORY_API_KEY in the environment
npx claude-mem import --from supermemory --source-account personal-supermemory --namespace my_namespace --project imported-memory
  • Start the worker first (npx claude-mem start). Add --dry-run to fetch and check the source and print counts without writing anything.
  • Every source page is fetched and checked before anything is written. Expired or replaced Mem0 memories and forgotten or older Supermemory memories are skipped. For Supermemory, --documents imports extracted document text instead of memories.
  • Imported memories are filed for Claude Code (claude), so its memory search finds them. --platform <host> (for example codex or cursor) files them under another host. Each observation keeps the source record, ID, timestamps, metadata, account label and scope.
  • Running the same command again is safe: records already saved are counted as existing. There is no background job and no automatic retry.
  • This is a one-way import, not a sync. Edits at the source make new observations. Deletions and expirations at the source are not carried over.
  • Limits: 10,000 records by default (--max-records up to 100,000), 100 MiB of source responses, a 15-second request deadline (--timeout-ms up to 120,000) and 100,000 characters per record. Nothing is cut short silently: an oversized record or a failed request stops the run.
  • The tests use synthetic Mem0 and Supermemory responses, not live accounts.

Docs: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/import-providers

Codex: forked threads get memory

  • Forked Codex threads start with recalled memory (#6101). Codex 0.165 added a fork session start for its experimental attached thread forks. claude-mem's SessionStart hook didn't match it, so a forked thread started with no memory. The hook now matches fork.

    Codex users: approve one hook again. The SessionStart hook's matcher changed, and Codex asks for approval again whenever a hook's definition changes.

    1. Get the new matcher into ~/.codex/hooks.json. npx claude-mem update and auto-update do this when your last install selected Codex. Otherwise run npx claude-mem install and select Codex.
    2. Open interactive Codex, run /hooks, and approve claude-mem's SessionStart hook.

    Until you approve it, Codex sessions start without recalled memory. Capture keeps working. Until the new matcher is in hooks.json, npx claude-mem doctor shows the Codex hooks row as out of date.

Also new

  • Server runtime: search results say which agent made a memory (#6100). The server runtime now stores the agent on each memory and fills it in for existing memories from their session. Its MCP search and detail lines add [via <agent>], for example #8 — Auth redirect decision (myproject) [via cursor]. Memories with no recorded agent show no tag. /api/sessions/observations no longer labels every client as Claude Code. The local worker's observation results don't carry the agent yet, so they show no tag.
  • Zed (#6111, thanks @AdityaxDeore, closes #5900). npx claude-mem install (or --ide zed) registers claude-mem's MCP server in Zed's context_servers, for search, timeline, details and explicit saves. Comments in Zed's settings file are kept. There is no automatic capture, because Zed has no hooks or transcript access. Docs: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/zed-integration
  • Aider (#6112, thanks @AdityaxDeore, closes #5893). Run npx claude-mem aider install inside a project. It adds .claude-mem/aider-memory.md to the read: list in .aider.conf.yml, and npx claude-mem aider sync refreshes that file from the worker. It is opt-in per project: npx claude-mem install doesn't offer it, the memory file is kept out of git through .git/info/exclude, and it refuses to run in your home folder. No automatic capture. Docs: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/aider-integration
  • Grok Build gets recalled memory at session start (#6180, thanks @krishnadobhal, closes #5950). Grok Build ignores what SessionStart hooks print, so recalled notes never reached the model. claude-mem grok install writes .grok/rules/claude-mem-context.md in the current folder, which Grok Build loads from trusted folders. The worker refreshes it after each session summary, only in folders you installed it in. An excluded project gets an "excluded" line instead of notes. Capture is unchanged. Docs: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/grok-build
  • French in the language picker for My Work, the viewer, first-run setup and Observation TV (#6107, thanks @QuantScorpus). Your memories, rules and quotes stay as written.
  • Three new presets for the OpenAI-compatible provider. Each defaults to a small, fast model, because memory extraction is high volume:
    • AtmoRouter, zai/glm-5.3-flash (#6108, thanks @BeckleyTenriajeng)
    • TrustedRouter, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash (#6174, thanks @jperla). trustedrouter/auto stays available as an opt-in. It can route a request to a model priced at frontier rates.
    • HopBase, deepseek-v4.1-flash (#6181, thanks @victor-zzh)

Fixes

Privacy and security

  • The claude-mem data folder is owner-only (#6091, thanks @DeryFerd). On macOS and Linux, ~/.claude-mem (database, settings, .env, hook spool, backups) was created with a plain mkdir, so under the common 022 umask other accounts on the machine could read it. It is now created as 0700, an existing folder is tightened on the next start, and new hook spool entries are written as 0600.
  • MCP save_memory honors CLAUDE_MEM_EXCLUDED_PROJECTS (#6105, thanks @Zhong-fan, reported by @Kirat0201 in #6098; @0xABCD01 sent the same fix in #6166). A save from an excluded checkout was stored over MCP while the same save over HTTP was skipped. It is skipped now, and the reply says "Not saved: this checkout is excluded by CLAUDE_MEM_EXCLUDED_PROJECTS." instead of "Saved memory #?: Untitled.". The Cline and Kilo guides now say so (#6190).
  • Server runtime: the MCP connect command refuses an unusable Host (#6176, thanks @DeryFerd). Without CLAUDE_MEM_PUBLIC_URL, GET /v1/connect and POST /v1/keys built the paste-ready command from the request's Host header and copied whitespace, quotes or paths into it. A value that cannot be a host now gets 400 InvalidHost, and no key is minted.
  • Sync hub: FORWARD_ORIGIN must use https:// (#6175, thanks @DeryFerd). The forward proxy copies the incoming Authorization header to the target, so a plain http:// origin could send it without TLS. http:// is allowed only for loopback hosts. A value that isn't a usable URL now fails loudly instead of quietly falling back to the Durable Object path.

Install and uninstall

  • Uninstall removes the Gemini CLI hooks (#6088, thanks @tanishqbaweja). npx claude-mem uninstall deleted the plugin but left claude-mem's five Gemini CLI hooks in ~/.gemini/settings.json, so Gemini CLI printed a failed-hook message at every session start, prompt, tool call and turn end. Uninstall now removes them and keeps your own settings and hooks. A settings.json with comments is left untouched, so remove those hooks by hand.
  • Cancelling the API-key prompt no longer switches you to Claude (#6161, thanks @bulanovk). With --provider gemini or --provider openrouter and no saved key, cancelling the key prompt wrote CLAUDE_MEM_PROVIDER='claude' and carried on. It now stops with an error and changes nothing.
  • The Codex installer's legacy-config check expands a leading ~\ only on Windows, like the rest of claude-mem (#6093, thanks @DeryFerd).

Worker and storage

  • A worker that meets a busy database at startup retries instead of answering 503 for minutes (#6145, thanks @montjeffrey, refs #3603). A replacement worker could hit SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT once during database startup, never retry, and answer every request with "Service initializing" until a manual restart (about 11 minutes in the report). Startup now retries a busy error 3 times, after 1, 2 and 4 seconds. The worst case (27 s) fits inside the 30 s the hook waits for the worker to be ready. Other errors still fail at once.
  • Closing the database releases it (#6090, thanks @DeryFerd). Cached prepared statements kept the connection and the database file open after close. On Windows that blocked restore swaps and temp-folder cleanup with EPERM or EBUSY.
  • Chroma cleanup for deleted sessions survives a worker exit (#6163, thanks @Afloat16). If the worker exited before the queued cleanup ran, the deleted rows' vectors were never removed. The cleanup is now recorded before it starts. The same change fixes a check that treated a missing row as restored on Bun.
  • On Bun, a database whose sync launch exclusions table went missing rebuilds it instead of keeping an empty list (#6189).
  • A failing /api/ready subscriber no longer stops startup progress for the others or turns into a startup failure (#6127, thanks @Afloat16).

Capture and memory notes

  • CLAUDE_MEM_SKIP_BASH_PATTERNS applies to Antigravity CLI (#6096, thanks @tanishqbaweja). agy reports its shell tool as run_command, which the pattern check didn't read, so excluded commands were stored and sent to the observer.
  • An explicit note containing a null character could get another note's ID while its own text was not saved (#6170, thanks @Kirat0201, closes #6169).
  • A Claude Code memory file whose description or metadata.type changed is stored as a new revision instead of being reported as already imported (#6186, thanks @Kirat0201, closes #6171).
  • Memory notes (thanks @Afloat16):
    • A note's title comes from its real headings, not from a # comment inside a code example (#6156).
    • Fields nested under a note's metadata: no longer overwrite the note's own type or session, and a YAML comment no longer ends the block (#6157).
    • memory ingest --source or --cwd with no value stops with a usage error instead of importing the current checkout (#6150).
    • Scanning a transcript again no longer inserts an imported turn twice when two nearby turns have the same text (#6149).
    • With CLAUDE_MEM_DEDUP_ENABLED=true, titles that differ only in code characters (C++ and C#, src/config.ts and src config ts, version numbers) are no longer merged into one row, which lost the second one (#6120).
    • Imported observations whose facts or files were stored as one string show them in recall again (#6134).

Search and context (thanks @Afloat16 unless noted)

  • Semantic search checks date windows against the saved rows, not Chroma's copy, so a row updated in SQLite but not yet in Chroma lands in the right window (#6153).
  • File lookups ordered by date skip Chroma, so a Chroma outage or slow embedding no longer fails them (#6123).
  • File context returns the newest observations when several share a timestamp (#6118).
  • The context cache keeps the right invalidation scope when renders finish out of order, so a later write in an adopted project refreshes it (#6164).
  • Deep search gives its child process only the time actually left, so a clock step such as an NTP correction no longer causes an early empty timeout (#6177, thanks @DeryFerd).

Codex as the memory provider (thanks @Afloat16)

  • The 8 MiB protocol limit applies to each JSON line, not to everything buffered, so valid output is no longer rejected (#6119).
  • A closed stdin pipe during a turn fails that turn cleanly instead of escaping as an unhandled error (#6130).
  • A timed-out request no longer leaves an abort handler behind that could fail the next turn on a new app-server (#6133).

Smart file read

  • smart_outline no longer marks declarations next to an export on the same line as [exported] (#6141, thanks @liuyinchu).
  • Now indexed (thanks @Afloat16): anonymous export default functions, arrows and classes (#6151), Swift protocol methods and bodyless Scala methods (#6154), and Java @interface declarations and their elements (#6160).
  • Smart code search reads each file through one handle and stops at the 512 KiB cap, so a file replaced after the size check can't get past the limit (#6124, thanks @Afloat16).

My Work

  • The goals step uses the run's language (#6187, thanks @0xABCD01, closes #6185 reported by @Fly-onlyone). The language line reached every step except goals, so in #6185 147 English prompts produced Spanish goals. A first goals-only run with no language set can still guess. CLAUDE_MEM_WORK_VIEW_TEXT_LANGUAGE sets it.
  • Also in My Work (thanks @Afloat16):
    • A Jev answer cut off mid-body counts as an outage, not a permanent failure for that item, so the next refresh asks again (#6158).
    • A new git init, a new nested repository or a removed .git is picked up the next time My Work works out a session's project, instead of only after a worker restart (#6165).
    • Auto-clear ignores late reads from a turn or conversation that already ended (#6152).
    • Owner prompts keep their full 3,000-character budget when they contain emoji and other characters outside the basic plane (#6162).
    • The opt-in API corpus agent matches accented, Hindi, Bengali and pointed Hebrew words (#6168).
    • Gemini usage totals in setup keep the completed token count when the same response was saved twice (#6146).

Viewer

  • Opening a viewer window sends its first project list and status only to that window, not to every open viewer (#6126, thanks @Afloat16).
  • Clicking the session actions button again closes its menu (#6143, thanks @liuyinchu).

Other

  • agent-cost-report writes CHECKSUMS.txt with forward slashes on Windows (#6089, thanks @DeryFerd).

Performance (thanks @Afloat16)

  • Long transcript lines are assembled once instead of copied on every read pass, in the backward reader (#6116) and the live watcher (#6117).
  • OpenCode prompt history is read one message at a time (#6121).
  • Large tool payloads are capped and hashed without full copies (#6128).
  • Timelines load only the rows they show (#6129). Recent sessions use an indexed summary check (#6132). Date formatters are reused within a render (#6125).
  • Project-scoped recall stops a merge check at the first unadopted row (#6131). The project catalog removes duplicates with sets (#6135). Long pasted queries stop scanning at the 500-term cap (#6147).
  • Smart file read finds each symbol's container with an index instead of a scan (#6122).
  • My Work indexes provenance records (#6148), focus request memberships (#6155) and work-state item versions (#6159) once per call.

Docs

  • Cline CLI and Kilo CLI guides for saving and finding memories through the stdio MCP server (#6097, #6114, thanks @Kirat0201). Docs: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/cline and https://docs.claude-mem.ai/kilo
  • Bundled skills drop ALWAYS and MANDATORY markers (#6183, thanks @jcole666, closes #6144 reported by @scu-lixiao).
  • The CMEM Pro endpoint spec defines a write:memory OAuth scope for hook ingest (#6099).

CI and tests

  • The Windows jobs (#6092) and the media runtime workflow (#6178) pin Bun 1.4.4 like the rest of CI (thanks @DeryFerd).
  • The work-view suites remove temp folders with the shared retry helper (#6094). The Windows lane runs both Python suites, and the Hermes suite is repaired (#6095) (thanks @DeryFerd).
  • A test pins the OpenCode 2.0 event names, so a renamed upstream event fails loudly (#6102).

View release →

v15.18.5 Stable2026-11-15T18:10:20Z

Critical fixes

  • The tree-sitter CLI installs on networks where its download script keeps failing (#6110, thanks @rigel905, closes #6109). On some networks tree-sitter-cli's own install.js had its request reset every time, or exited 0 on a truncated file. The pinned SHA-256 check correctly refused the file, but nothing recovered after that, so smart_search, smart_outline, smart_unfold and the File Read Gate stayed off on every worker start, and npx claude-mem repair aborted. Now, when the script fails or leaves anything but the pinned executable, claude-mem fetches the same release asset directly, once, inside the same install time budget, and runs it only after it unpacks to the same pinned SHA-256. The script still runs first, so HTTPS_PROXY keeps working. A script that used up the whole budget gets no second attempt.
  • A corrupt Chroma collection is dropped once, not once per parallel backfill (#6115, thanks @mohitdixit02 and @0xABCD01, closes #6113). When the HNSW segment of a large collection was corrupt, every parallel per-project backfill that hit it passed the "drop only once" check before the first delete finished, and queued its own delete against chroma-mcp. In #6113 that ran 19 drops at once and pushed chroma-mcp to a 312 GB memory footprint, stalling a 32 GB Mac. Callers now join the one drop already running for that collection and share its outcome. A failed drop costs one attempt from the retry budget, not one per caller, and different collections still drop independently. The remaining asks from that report (a memory bound on chroma-mcp, stopping writes when a drop can't be confirmed, measuring footprint on macOS) are tracked in #3610.

Fixes

  • --help prints help instead of running the command (#6142, thanks @liuyinchu). npx claude-mem mcp --help used to start the stdio server, and status, doctor and hook entered their runtime paths; t3code and its aliases rejected the flag. -h and --help are now handled before dispatch for these commands. Plain mcp still starts the server.

Docs

  • OmO Native recall guide (#6087, thanks @mschoi0411). How to connect OmO Native to the local worker through the existing stdio MCP server: tool discovery, recall by project and observation ID, troubleshooting and disconnect.

can1357/oh-my-pi ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v18.20.3 Stable2026-11-16T01:38:21Z

@oh-my-pi/pi-ai

Breaking Changes

  • Removed the public isXdDevicePath export from providers/cursor-pi-args. Ranged reads of xd:// documents now use the standard line-selector behavior.

Fixed

  • Fixed rate-limit handling for Mistral and other OpenAI-compatible providers so requests with no available allowance fail immediately with an actionable error suggesting a model or plan change.
  • Fixed Anthropic OAuth requests for pooled Claude accounts to report accurate device and account information, including after credentials are rotated during a request.

@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog

Added

  • Added publicly available image-sizing helpers for determining model-delivered image dimensions and fitting images to a specified long edge before coordinate mapping.

Fixed

  • Fixed image inputs being dropped for DeepSeek V4 Flash, restoring consistent multimodal image support.
  • Restricted reasoning-effort options for Mistral GLM 5.3, GLM 5.3 Flash, and Mistral Large 4 to the levels supported by those models.

@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent

Breaking Changes

  • Renamed the browser tab.clickAt() option from clickCount to count, matching tab.click().
  • Browser viewport screenshot coordinates now use the displayed image coordinates when the screenshot is scaled for the model; pass css: true (or { x, y, css: true } for drag points) to provide viewport CSS pixels explicitly.
  • Added opt-in mnemopi.recallRelevance (off, auto, or on; default off) to filter automatic memory recall for task relevance using the judge role.
  • Added path-scoped entries for bash.patterns and bashInterceptor.patterns, resolved per working directory. Project and --config overlays now prepend these rules to global rules instead of replacing them.
  • Added bash.allowedEnvVars and per-rule env lists to permit explicitly named environment-variable prefixes on matching allow rules.
  • Subagents now preserve @upstream provider pinning on inherited models.
  • Added --no-judge, --no-spotlight, and --offline options to restrict auxiliary services to the active model's provider or disable cross-provider services.
  • Added per-rule TTSR repeatMode frontmatter (once, after-gap, or always) to override the global repeat policy.
  • Compound bash approval prompts now show each command segment separately, distinguishing allowed segments from those requiring approval.
  • Removed the seance agent, /seance command, and the task tool's sourceSession parameter.

Added

  • Added mnemopi.embeddingQueryPrefix and mnemopi.embeddingInputType configuration for asymmetric and instruction-tuned embedding models, including providers that require an input_type.

Changed

  • Browser screenshots are delivered to the model in CSS pixels up to the supported unscaled size, making viewport screenshot coordinates directly usable with browser actions; scaling guidance remains for scaled full-page and element captures.
  • Browser waitForUrl, waitForResponse, and requests({ filter }) now support * glob patterns in URL strings, while other strings retain substring matching.
  • The WebKit browser engine now automatically installs and updates to the newest stable ABKit release, with versioned installations that allow updates without waiting for existing browser hosts to exit.
  • Improved browser responsiveness and recovery: unresponsive WebKit pages fail fast with actionable errors, navigation can recover busy pages, and browser operations provide clearer diagnostics for timeouts, closed tabs, unsupported event listeners, invalid routes, cookie data, and viewport changes.
  • Pressing Delete at the end of the Ctrl+R search field removes the selected prompt from history.
  • /copy now works while viewing a subagent and copies from that subagent's transcript.
  • find now returns unranked literal keyword matches when all judge requests fail.
  • take() and drop() now reject nonexistent hunk units with a clear error.
  • edit rejection messages now suggest the file's current tag, and edits made before conflict resolution carry over to the resolved file.
  • /marketplace and marketplace install/uninstall commands now report picker and catalog-load errors without exiting the session.
  • ACP sessions honor mcp.startupTimeoutMs for MCP servers declared by the client, and ACP form elicitations no longer repeat field labels unnecessarily.
  • Task progress from every task.steps subagent step is now preserved, rather than only the final step's report.
  • Pasting HTML into the composer now preserves spaces from whitespace-only inline elements and indentation inside <pre> blocks.
  • Queued follow-ups edited with Alt+Up are restored as queued messages instead of being sent into the active turn.

Fixed

  • Fixed ida exec output on IDA 9.5+ by suppressing helper deprecation warnings and preserving the updated function metadata API.
  • Expired Perplexity logins and cookies no longer return an error page as a search answer; the provider is reported as expired and the search chain continues.
  • Fixed browser WebMCP discovery and invocation on Chrome and Chromium 157 and later.
  • Private hosts written with a trailing dot are now correctly handled by Ask and always-ask-cached before file tools access them.
  • Fixed the TUI freezing when switching sessions from an open tool-approval prompt.
  • Fixed /commit and eval commit dropping UTF-8 BOMs or mishandling quoted and Unicode filenames during change tracking and selective commits.
  • Fixed misleading Wayland clipboard warnings when pasting an image or when the clipboard is empty.
  • Fixed JavaScript evaluation after an in-place Linux upgrade by keeping session workers tied to the session's build.
  • Deleting a session that cannot be removed no longer deletes its prompt history and statistics.
  • Fixed read and write handling of line selectors on xd:// device URLs.
  • Fixed eval wait() rejecting or mishandling numeric delays; browser waits now direct users to the appropriate wait helpers.
  • Fixed browser open with an existing Arch Chromium profile, Tern navigation, closed external Tern blocks, and docked Tern viewport emulation.
  • Fixed Tern and WebKit browser calls that incorrectly exposed unsupported page event-listener APIs; errors now identify the supported alternatives.
  • Fixed browser timeout and busy-page errors to include the current URL, affected tab, and actionable recovery guidance.
  • Fixed Mnemopi embedding failures being silently downgraded to keyword search; provider errors now produce a warning, including in print mode on stderr.

@oh-my-pi/pi-mnemopi

Added

  • Added configurable embedding query prefixes and input types for instruction-tuned and asymmetric embedding models, including Qwen3-Embedding, E5, and NVIDIA NIM.
  • Added the embeddings.onRequestFailed callback, allowing hosts to handle and surface failed embedding API requests.

@oh-my-pi/pi-natives

Fixed

  • Committing or writing trees now correctly reports unresolved index conflicts instead of silently omitting conflicted files.
  • Fixed shell compatibility with GNU grep for end-of-line-anchored patterns, including -o and -z modes, and corrected sed substitutions on multibyte-character lines.
  • Fixed native diff and patch handling for filenames containing spaces and other characters requiring quoting, including binary changes.

@oh-my-pi/pi-utils

Fixed

  • Fixed HTML-to-Markdown conversion for fetched and pasted HTML to preserve whitespace in inline elements, maintain code indentation in preformatted blocks, and avoid inserting stray blank lines between block elements.

What's Changed

  • fix(edit): offer the current tag for the rows shown when a header tag is unknown by @Xytronix in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/19332
  • fix(approval): gate private hosts written with a trailing dot by @XYZ1024-alt in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/19228
  • fix(find): list literal keyword matches when every judge request fails by @yuzu-octopus in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/19231

  • fix(coding-agent): kept retained snapshots when a conflict:// write resolves a block by @tuschla in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/19233
  • fix(coding-agent): report /marketplace picker load failures instead of crashing by @tuschla in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/19234
  • fix(browser): reuse Chromium started through a compiled launcher by @tuschla in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/19235
  • fix(coding-agent): closed pending tool approval when the turn aborts by @roboomp in https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/19242

pip install 'browser-use==1.0.6'

  • BU 4.0 is the default model. Agent(task) and ChatBrowserUse() now run bu-4.0 on the Browser Use gateway instead of bu-fast. Pass llm='bu-4.0-mini' for simple tasks at the lowest cost, or llm='bu-4.0-pro' for the hardest tasks (#6430).

BU 4.0 tokens cost 15 times as much as bu-fast ($1.80 / $9.00 per 1M input / output tokens, against $0.12 / $0.60), and it runs at high instead of medium reasoning in the default mode. A short test task cost $0.022 instead of $0.0014. To keep the previous model and price, pass llm='bu-fast'. Prices: https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/models
  • The first run without a key opens Browser Use login and continues after approval; cloud browsers print their live-view link (#6425).
  • Judge gotchas stay grounded in what the run observed (#6418).

kajisho5/ffmpeg-skill ↗ 3 releases · 3 stable
v3.10.1 Stable2026-11-15T23:32:49Z

Automated release: version and notes generated from pull requests merged since 3.10.0.

Fixed

  • A data stream the container refuses no longer costs the subtitle track beside it (#539). The tools that keep a source's subtitle and data streams through one helper (fit, color, crop, stabilize, graphics, overlay, audio, loudness, proxy, deinterlace, denoise, redact, sphere, straighten, pad --end, freeze of the last frame) retried without all of them when one failed: an MP4 with a mov_text track and a start timecode lost the track when written to .mkv, and on FFmpeg 6.1.1 to .mp4 too. The data stream is now retried away alone, as export.py does; the non_av_streams_dropped fallback carries dropped, the stream types left out, and for a source with a subtitle and a data stream dropped_non_av_streams is false when the MP4 muxer wrote the timecode track itself (a source with a data stream and no subtitle still reports true after its retry). color.py --retag's re-encode fallback has its own copy step and is not changed.
  • metadata.py refuses a stream the output container cannot take as a copy, before ffmpeg runs (#539). A SubRip MKV written to .mp4 (a mov_text MP4 to .mkv, a timecode track to Matroska, an attachment outside Matroska) failed inside ffmpeg after a dry run that said completed; it is kind: input now, a dry run included, with a hint naming export.py --preset copy. An MP4 with a start timecode, which FFmpeg 6.1.1 would not copy even into .mp4, is written: the timecode track alone is left out of the copy and the muxer writes it again (.m4v too). .m4a is judged as the MPEG-4 family it is: sound with a SubRip track is refused there as well.
  • A tool that writes a picture refuses an audio-only output extension (#539). fit, pad, speedramp, reverse, loop and the other picture tools completed with H.264 inside -o x.m4a and failed in the muxer for -o x.wav. Both are refused before ffmpeg runs (kind: input, reason output_extension_audio_only), dry runs included; metadata.py refuses it for a source with a picture, and waveform.py's own refusal carries the same reason. A stream copy by sync.py --replace-audio is not covered.
  • An audio output of audio.py or loudness.py keeps a late sound in place (#539). A source whose sound starts after its picture was written from the sound's first sample, so a .wav, .flac or .m4a extraction played that much early. The lead is written as silence, as cut.py --accurate writes it, for the track --audio-stream selects, and reaches the encoder in frames of 4096 samples (FFmpeg 9's FLAC encoder refused the one large frame the pad produced). Beside a copied picture nothing changes.
  • graphics.py's 0.3 s fades and the lower third's slide fit a short window (#539). In a --start/--end window under 0.3 s the text never faded out, and between 0.3 and 0.6 s its brightness jumped; the lower third's bar jumped back in a window under 0.7 s. Each fade is cut to half the window and the slide shares it 4:3, on drawtext and on the ASS route; the sticker's pop is cut with its fade on both routes, and a lower third whose slides fill the window draws no rest phase (its emoji showed for one frame).

Checked on FFmpeg 6.1.1 (Linux) only. Left open in #539 for a decision: caption.py's burn and waveform.py drop the source's subtitle track, and cut.py -o x.mka re-encodes a picture into the .mka.

  • fix: a refused stream costs only itself, and an output is what its name says (#554)

What's Changed

  • fix: a refused stream costs only itself, and an output is what its name says by @kajisho5 in https://github.com/kajisho5/ffmpeg-skill/pull/554

v3.10.0 Stable2026-11-15T19:04:53Z

Changed

  • A render.py project of several clips takes its picture size from the fit object, as a one-clip project does, in the render and in --export-timeline (#526). fit.py gets the fit object's aspect, mode, width and height and the frame's only where the object has none, and the exported sequence (FCPXML, EDL, OTIO) is sized, and timed, from the same merge. Before, a multi-clip render fitted the object inside the joined picture and the export sized the sequence from frame alone, so the two disagreed. Over two 160x120 clips: frame 16:9 with fit 1:1 rendered 120x120 against a 160x90 sequence (now both 120x120); frame {aspect 16:9, width 320} with fit {aspect 4:5, fit crop} rendered 192x240 against 320x180 (now 320x400); frame 1:1 with fit {width 200} exported 120x120 (now 200x200, as rendered); frame {width 320, height 180} with fit 1:1 rendered 180x180 (now 320x180, as exported: two sides given are kept, as for one clip); frame 16:9 at 25 fps with fit {fps 24} exported a 25 fps sequence (now 24, as rendered). A frame of one side now gives join.py the other side rounded as fit.py rounds it: {width 100} over 4:3 clips rendered 100x74 against a 100x76 sequence (now 100x76). Where the fit object gives that side itself the join is sized from it ({width 100} with fit {width 200}: 200x150 both), and a key the fit object gives as null counts as not given, in the render as in the export. The clips are joined at the rate the render delivers, the fit object's where it gives one: joined at the frame's 25 fps and conformed to fit {fps 24}, two 0.7 s clips rendered 35 frames against a 34-frame sequence. A multi-clip export now refuses a fit.aspect or fit.fit that fit.py refuses, as a one-clip export already did. One-clip projects render and export as before. Which multi-clip projects change is listed in docs/design-decisions.md ("After 3.9.3").

code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent ↗ 2 releases · 2 stable
v5.1.72 Stable2026-11-15T21:51:26Z

A thread send now reaches a session that is not running, on this device or on another of your devices, and starts it. It needs senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (omo pins it), and device service 0.1.31 or later on both devices for a wake from another device. A reply to a sender on another device reads only that device's sessions instead of the whole account listing; a send to a live session that is paused or holds a Stop answers queued with waiting_on: { kind: "hold", device }; and waiting_on.kind in a thread_send result can be approval, hold or wake. (#13599)

Changed

  • omo remote enable now sets the device up in one command after omo login. It installs the OmO device service when none runs, registers this omo's agent dir with it, turns remote sessions on, and installs and starts the always-on session host unit. If you signed in before the device service was installed, it also links that sign-in to the service, so omo login then omo remote enable leaves the device connected. Running it again changes nothing that is already in place (#13594). (#13602) (#13606)
  • omo remote status also shows this device's own units as the service manager reports them: the session host unit (running, enabled, pinned host), the device service's unit, whether the cold-wake entry is in place, and the agent dir omo registers. With --json these are a local object beside the status fields (#13594). (#13602) (#13606)
  • Thread gateway: waking a session that is not running is on (#13037). It runs on senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (omo now pins it), the release whose session release drops a woken session's retained record. A message from another of your devices wakes a session here once both devices run device service 0.1.31 or later. The local omo daemon (omo daemon run, or the device service's cold-wake unit) registers this device's agent dir with the device service and takes deliveries as soon as it starts, with no session open. (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: the operator daemon declares the delivery consumer as soon as it loads omo, with no session open (#13037 cold wake). omo daemon run sends the daemon it ensured senpi's warm, so a daemon the device service starts on demand can be handed deliveries before any session runs. A warm that is refused or unsupported prints one line and the run still exits 0. (#13596) (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: the session wake loads from its own sidecar (extensions/omo-wake.js behind #omo-wake-runtime): the carrier, the delivery consumer and the device-service client never enter the main omo.js bundle, which carries only lazy shells; the ensured host's idle-exit setting is read inside the sidecar. (#13456) (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: waking a session that is not running needs no setting (#13037). A thread_send from this machine to a session here that is not running now starts it by default, and the answer is queued with waiting_on: { kind: "wake" }. session_wake.same_device stays in the configuration schema only as an explicit opt-out (false), read for the target session's own project. The wake starts on senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (senpi#6449), which omo now pins. (#13456) (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: when no operator host is running, a session that is not running still starts (#13037). Before it opens the session, the carrier asks the engine's own host ensure --policy never, from omo's daemon launch spec, on the socket thread_create uses. A running host is reused whatever its build; one is started only when nothing answers. The ensured host runs with omo daemon's own host environment: the agent directory is named (OMO_AGENT_DIR) and the configured task.host_idle_exit_ms rides along (SENPI_RPC_HOST_IDLE_EXIT_MS) instead of the launch spec's default, and from a source tree the launch spec resolves to the plugin's tracked copy so the CLI is always handed a file that exists. (#13456) (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: a delivery from another device is no longer gated on the device service's wake switch being told on. While this engine's delivery consumer is served (from its serving acknowledgement, before its startup pending sweep, so a remote row that sweep wakes is never told the gate is off), the carrier opens the session. The consumer serves on senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later with device service 0.1.31 or later, and it no longer reads the wake the service tells: the wake switch it tracked (wakeAllowed, the delivery.wake event) had no production reader left. (#13456) (#13599)
  • The delivery consumer (design 5.4) runs beside the carrier. The engine minimum for a woken session, MIN_WAKE_ENGINE_VERSION (A8.1, senpi 2026.11.15-2, the release that drops a released session's retained record), gates the carrier as well. A device service older than 0.1.31 does not carry the delivery protocol, so on it the consumer serves nothing and does not ask again. (#13455) (#13599)
  • The gateway store's schema moves to version 12: three nullable columns on deliveries and a unique index on the new ledger id. The first process on this release migrates the store; any process still on the previous build then reports the store's "schema too new" error on its thread tools and inbox drain until it restarts. (#13208) (#13279) (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: once a build carrying this store ships, every gateway store open runs the schema step to version 13 (one new table, woken_sessions) and raises the store's user_version for good. An older build, or a rolled-back one, that shares the same agent directory then refuses to open that store with its "schema too new" error until it is upgraded again. (#13212) (#13279) (#13599)
  • A reply to a message that came from another of your devices goes to the session on that device that sent it, whether you reply by its session id or by the name it gave. A session on another device, or on this one, that only carries the same id or name no longer receives the reply. (#13218, part of #13037) (#13599)

Fixed

  • An omo engine on a device whose device service runs on a non-default --state-dir now registers with it: deviceServiceStateDir takes a non-empty absolute OMO_DEVICE_SERVICE_STATE_DIR, then the device-service.location.json discovery file beside the default dir, and only then ~/.omo/device-service (#13597). (#13598) (#13606)
  • A remote worktree remove refused for an empty reflog now says reflogs may be off in the repository, instead of claiming they are: an expired or deleted reflog looks the same (#13542 follow-up). (#13546) (#13606)
  • Thread gateway: the session wake keeps working after the session that started it ends (#13037). The carrier and the delivery consumer are one per agent directory for the whole process, but they used the first session's gateway store, which that session's shutdown closed, so every later wake in the process failed. The running wake now opens its own store for the life of the process. (#13596) (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: the carrier re-checks the sender's peer admission at the moment of every open of a row from another device (#13456 review follow-up), so the retry and lease-takeover paths - which the accept-time check of the consumer and the before-turn check of the drain bracketed but nothing else covered - start nothing when the answer is refused or unknown. A lease takeover now consults the same allowance a wake does, ending its record when nothing queued allows the open; the runtime answers the carrier's admission ask on the live delivery port, so the startup pending sweep's own wakes are admitted too. (#13511) (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: the session wake loads from its own sidecar (extensions/omo-wake.js behind #omo-wake-runtime): the carrier, the delivery consumer and the device-service client never enter the main omo.js bundle, which carries only lazy shells. (#13457) (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: a consumer failure that changes kind (a device that answers nothing and then refuses the declaration) is warned again: the retry loop's one-warning rule is keyed on the failure itself, not on merely being down, and still stays silent while the same failure repeats. (#13457) (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: the delivery consumer listens before it declares itself, so the records the device service hands it right after the acknowledgement are no longer dropped. It counts as serving from that acknowledgement, so a session it wakes during its own start is opened, not left switched off. (#13457) (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: the delivery consumer is started again after it dies (#13457 review): a device service that answers nothing, refuses the declaration, or restarts under a served connection no longer leaves remote wake off for the engine's life. A failed start closes its port and reports itself, a connection that ends during the startup sweep leaves no stale serving consumer behind, and a connect failure the client reports is logged instead of dropped. (#13457) (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: the wake switch the service tells (delivery.wake) has no reader since the carrier's gate moved to the consumer serving, so the consumer no longer tracks it. The conformance fakes the production-port test uses are now a package export of device-service-core instead of a deep path into its test tree. (#13457) (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: a delivery id that the same device repeats after its 30-day receipt expired, while its row is still in the store, is answered from that row as deduplicated instead of failing with a raw unique-constraint error (the review of #13208). (#13212) (#13279) (#13599)
  • Thread gateway: a session whose file header cannot be read, or names a session kind this build does not know, is never started or reopened unattended. It is refused like a child or worker session instead of being treated as an ordinary interactive one (#13037). (#13279) (#13599)
  • When another device refuses to wake a session there that is not running, the reason its delivery consumer gives is shown only when it is a short machine code; any other reason is shown as unrecognised. (#13277, part of #13037) (#13599)

Added

  • omo remote bootstrap and omo remote enable install and start one fixed, always-on per-user unit beside the OmO device service that runs the omo session host: the systemd user unit omo-session-host.service on Linux (enabled, restarted after every exit) and the LaunchAgent ai.omo.session-host on macOS (run at load, kept alive). It runs omo daemon run --pinned for the registered agent dir, and the device service's OMO_RELAYD_SERVICES table names it (entry "omo") as the only unit it may start for a cold wake. The table keeps its other entries, and the device service restarts only when the table changed. omo remote disable disables and removes both, and while remote sessions are off a bootstrap removes them instead of installing them (#13594). (#13595) (#13606)

  • omo daemon run --pinned starts the operator host with no idle exit; a task host started from one of its sessions still idles out as usual (#13594). (#13595) (#13606)

  • Device service client: the delivery-consumer requests of #13037 (deliveries.serve, delivery.answer, delivery.held, delivery.pending, delivery.drained, peer.admitted) and their events (delivery.inbound, delivery.holds, delivery.wake), in the shapes omo-relay-daemon #1076 ships, behind connectDeliveryConsumer in device-service-core. The conformance fixtures are copied in-tree from that release. (#13457) (#13599)

  • Thread gateway: the engine's delivery consumer now connects to the device service through that client, so a delivery from another device for a session here that is not running is taken in, answered, and the session started. (#13457) (#13599)

  • Thread gateway: the session wake now loads from its own sidecar, extensions/omo-wake.js behind #omo-wake-runtime: the carrier and its host connection, the delivery consumer and the device-service client never enter the main omo.js bundle, which carries only three lazy shells (the session-start start, a send's same-device wake, the control endpoint's admission ask); a sidecar that fails to load answers as if no wake exists. Measured 1,547,852 -> 1,476,860 bytes on this branch; the byte ceiling in bundle-budget.json moves to 1,478,000 for it. (#13455) (#13599)

  • Thread gateway: the session wake of #13037 now runs in production, but only on an engine at or above the wake engine minimum MIN_WAKE_ENGINE_VERSION (A8.1): the first engine release that drops a woken session's retained record (senpi#6449). Below it no carrier starts, and a thread_send naming a session that is not running answers as it did before the wake existed (queued_offline with reason: "wake_unavailable"). At or above it, every tui or rpc engine (never a task child, never under CI) starts one carrier per agent directory on its first session start: it opens the session by path on the operator host that thread_create opens on, sends the engine's wake, and hands it back quietly once it has finished; the answer is then queued with waiting_on: { kind: "wake" }. It still follows session_wake.same_device, read for the target session's own project, which stays off by default. (#13455) (#13599)

  • Thread gateway: the carrier sweeps its woken rows on a timer only while the table holds a row (design A3.1.4: an empty table leaves no timer). (#13455) (#13599)

  • Thread gateway: a session's own inbox drain admits nothing while a carrier is opening it (A3.1.5). It asks the device service whether a row's sending device is admitted before it takes in a delivery from another device (5.6). (#13455) (#13599)

  • Thread gateway: the store can take in a delivery that another device's service attested for a session on this device that is not running (the intake row of #13037). The row is committed in the same transaction as a same-device delivery, keeps the sender's delivery id, text and display text, is rate-limited per sending device, and is admitted later under the engine's own ledger key, so the engine counts it once even if the same delivery also arrives live. A repeat of a delivery id from the same device is answered with the first answer. A reply to such a delivery continues its chain. (#13208) (#13279) (#13599)

  • Thread gateway: the store keeps a record of each session a wake asked for or opened (#13037): one row with its state, a lease and a generation that fences every write, at most 4 such sessions past requested per agent directory, and a transient open failure that returns the row to requested with its attempts and the time of the next one (the third deletes it). A wake primitive resolves a durable id to its one session file, refuses child and worker sessions, ensures the host and sends one plain open_session frame (no attended, no permission preset). (#13212) (#13279) (#13599)

  • Thread gateway: the pieces that will let a message from another of your signed-in devices reach a session that is not running on this device are the delivery consumer, the carrier that opens such a session in its own working directory and hands it back when its turn is done, and the pending sweep (#13037). (#13220) (#13279) (#13599)

  • omo remote wake [on|off|default] reads or sets whether sessions on this device that are not running may be started by a message from your other signed-in devices; default follows the build's default, which is off. It needs device service 0.1.31 or later; on an older one the command sends nothing and says so. (#13257, part of #13037) (#13599)

v5.1.71 Stable2026-11-15T15:58:45Z

The builtin architect category now defaults to Claude Fable 5.2 at thinking level xhigh instead of max: both chain rungs (the 5.2 lead and the 5.1 fallback, kept as the fallback at the same effort) carry xhigh, verified against the engine model catalog per the #9378 rule. Docs that spell the builtin default follow. Other categories, agent chains, and model profiles are unchanged (#13543). (#13545) (#13563)

Memory sync names the last unexplained "authority is unavailable" causes, and its log stays free of memory text. When closing a sync operation, releasing its claim, or the request handler itself failed, Settings still showed the bare "Memory sync authority is unavailable." with nothing in the log. These now carry a code (close_failed, release_failed, handler_failed) and log a warning. Logged errors name the error type, not its message; only a sync service error keeps its service code and status, because other messages can quote memory content. A device or pending-request read whose failure returns after the service refused a request is logged again. Carried by the next train top's bundle regeneration. (#13332, follow-up to #13157) (#13563)

A signed-out desktop no longer looks like a memory-sync error to the engine. When the desktop had no signed-in account, the engine's main thread treated the desktop's refusal as a broken channel and the sync runner reported an error; it now reads it as signed out, as session Workers already did, and picks up the account once you sign in. Carried by the next train top's bundle regeneration. (#13329, follow-up to #13325) (#13563)

Memory sync keeps working when you sign out and back in on the desktop. Signing out and signing in again (with the same or another account) while the engine runs used to leave Settings > Memory > Sync on "Memory sync authority is unavailable." until the engine restarted. The engine now ends only the old account when the desktop retires it, ends that account's open sync sessions once, and picks up the new account on the next status read. It needs a desktop that keeps the private channel open across the rollover; with an older desktop the behaviour is unchanged. Carried by the next train top's bundle regeneration. (#13327, fixes #13325) (#13563)

omo remote accepts -- to end its options. omo remote send <device>/<session> -- --text that starts with dashes now sends that text, and the same works for a model id given to omo remote model; before, any argument starting with -- was refused as an unknown option. Options before -- still apply. (#13496, fixes #13431)

The omo remote reference matches the command again. It lists open, send, model, interrupt and close with their flags, and describes attach as a view you can type into; it no longer says the attach view is observe-only. The Senpi plugin README lists all 27 skills it ships (it said 19). (#13492, fixes #13433)

omo remote --help and omo remote <command> --help now answer. They print the usage (or that command's entry with its flags) on stdout and exit 0, before any sign-in or device-service check, instead of failing as an unknown argument. omo --help lists remote among the commands. -h now also answers as a help flag after any verb, including in a value position (for example omo remote open dev --project --help prints help instead of taking --help as the project name). (#13489, fixes #13405)

omo-opencode tests no longer depend on the order test files run in. Under bun, module mocks leaked into later test files whenever files ran in sorted order (as bun test --shard runs them): six tmux-utils tests replaced modules with partial mocks, two modules that tests mock re-exported functions (the team-mode member resolver's dependencies and the legacy plugin toast's entry migrator), and two claude-code-hooks tests module-mocked shared modules. The tmux mocks are now complete, those two modules define their own forwarding functions so a mock of them stays scoped, and dispatch-hook.test.ts and execute-http-hook-security.test.ts use spies that are restored after each test. Tests, plus two forwarding-only source changes (features/team-mode/team-runtime/resolve-member-dependencies.ts and hooks/legacy-plugin-toast/plugin-entry-migrator.ts); no runtime behaviour changes. (#13333, fixes #13331)

Changed

  • OmO now pins @code-yeongyu/senpi and its packages at 2026.11.15. That senpi release brings the permission-prompt abort fix, the tool-result slash-command injection fix, sign-in-with-ChatGPT scope and input fixes, and the binary update that reads the GitHub release. (#13563)
  • Daily · Normal now walks Claude Opus 5.5 (medium), then Claude Fable 5.2 (medium), then Kimi K3.1 Pro (max), matching senpi's shipped Opus 5.5 fallback chain; GLM 5.3 is no longer a Daily · Normal rung, so a GLM-only setup gets no automatic Daily · Normal model (#13562). (#13562) (#13563)
  • Daily · Heavy runs Claude Fable 5.2 at high (was xhigh); its Fable 5.1 rung stays at xhigh (#13562). (#13562) (#13563)
  • @oh-my-opencode/utils no longer exports migrateConfigFile from its package root or from its migration entry point (@oh-my-opencode/utils/migration): the re-export in packages/utils/src/migration.ts is removed, and the root entry re-exports that module. Nothing imported it through either entry. The function itself is unchanged. (#13544) (#13563)
  • Internal: omo remote status and session commands now read the account without loading the code that signs in or refreshes, and reach the device service through the local API client directly. Nothing changes for users; this prepares a faster start for these commands (#13440). (#13477) (#13563)
  • The gateway store's schema moves to version 12: three nullable columns on deliveries and a unique index on the new ledger id. The first process on this release migrates the store; any process still on the previous build then reports the store's "schema too new" error on its thread tools and inbox drain until it restarts. (#13208) (#13279) (#13563)
  • Thread gateway: once a build carrying this store ships, every gateway store open runs the schema step to version 13 (one new table, woken_sessions) and raises the store's user_version for good. An older build, or a rolled-back one, that shares the same agent directory then refuses to open that store with its "schema too new" error until it is upgraded again. (#13212) (#13279) (#13563)
  • The standalone omo binary starts about 4x faster on Linux and 6x faster on macOS: release binaries now carry Bun's bytecode cache, so a launch no longer parses the whole bundled program first (omo --version 880 ms -> 202 ms on Linux x64, 214 ms -> 33 ms on Apple silicon). Each binary is about 43 MB larger, and the per-binary size budget rises from 210 MiB to 260 MiB. (#13464)

Fixed

  • The remote worktree remove guard's comment no longer claims a failed open's worktree always has exactly one reflog entry: a repo with core.logAllRefUpdates off reports none even for a branch just made, so there the worktree is refused worktree_left_behind and stays for its local owner; a test pins that refusal (#13450 follow-up). (#13542) (#13563)
  • The bundle marker digest no longer folds the running node's builtinModules into the digested build settings: the builtin family is recorded as one stable token and only source-derived externals are digested, so a byte-identical bundle built under node 26 (which adds node:ffi) no longer reads as stale. A RED test pins the stability and that a source-derived external still changes the digest (#13155). (#13541) (#13563)
  • A memory reflection or dream launcher now hears its supervisor's exit even when the supervisor dies while the "launched" receipt is still being written. The launcher used to subscribe to the exit only after that write, so an early supervisor death was never reported and the launcher waited for an outcome that could not arrive: until the run deadline (15 minutes by default), or without a deadline while the run was still queued. The run now fails at once with the supervisor's exit status. (#13532) (#13563)
  • An engine registers its agent dir with the device service again when the service stops and comes right back, whether or not the operating system reports the new socket in time. Once its connection had closed, the registrant used to wait for that file notification alone, and on a macOS machine with heavy file activity the notification arrived seconds to tens of seconds late, so the restarted service did not list that engine's sessions until then. The registrant now arms its endpoint watch again once the endpoint it knew is gone, so a service that is listening again within about a second of that is found by the watch's one-second re-check. A service that returns later than that still waits for the notification (#13531) (#13530, fixes #12733). (#13563)
  • An in-process child session's shutdown now waits for the session's own whenToolChildClosed() barrier after dispose() before its caller removes the directory that child's agent dir lives in, so a still-pending engine writer can no longer recreate that directory after the removal. The split-local, gated-child and permission-event test fixtures gained the same join, plus a held-writer regression case that proves the teardown does not settle while the writer is held (#13522). (#13522) (#13563)
  • thread_create on another device with a file as cwd now answers invalid_arguments (not_a_directory, naming the device and the path) once that device's engine refuses it (session_cwd_not_directory, code-yeongyu/senpi#6686), instead of an "update omo" refusal. (#13488, refs #13400) (#13563)
  • Thread tools: thread_create no longer notes that a new thread is outside the caller's workspace when the caller has no workspace at all (scoped addressing then answers caller_context_missing, not a workspace refusal). (#13462) (#13563)
  • A thread no engine runs on this device (closed, or its terminal exited) answers every thread tool the way a send to it does: thread_read reads its session file (source: "session_jsonl"), and thread_interrupt, thread_rename, thread_set_model and thread_set_reasoning answer not_resumable, the same refusal a thread that ended on another device gets, instead of not_found while thread_send queued to it. (#13459) (#13563)
  • thread_create on this device answers the same thread summary as on another device (id, name, folder, state, times and link) instead of the engine's whole session state. (#13459) (#13563)
  • thread_create on this device in a folder outside the caller's workspace says so: the result adds workspace_scope: "outside" and scope_next_action, because every thread tool answers that thread scope_denied unless all_scope is set. (#13459) (#13563)
  • A thread tool call that fails (thread_list, thread_send and the rest, plus extension store tools) now returns isError: true, so the engine and the eval bridge report it as failed instead of as a success. The typed failure, with its code and next action, is unchanged. (#13451, fixes #13398) (#13563)
  • A thread thread_create makes on another device is named by its durable id; the relay listing key it returned before answered not_found in every later thread tool (#13393). (#13450) (#13563)
  • thread_create's cwd: a relative folder resolves against the caller's folder on this device and is refused on another device, and a folder that does not exist answers invalid_arguments naming it, on both devices, instead of internal_error or "update omo" (#13400). (#13450) (#13563)
  • thread_create on another device that opened the session but could not name its relay key or apply its name answers the created thread with thread.warnings instead of an error, so a retry replays it and a new key cannot create a second session. (#13450) (#13563)
  • thread_create { fork_from } is refused unsupported (details.reason: fork_unsupported) on both devices instead of opening a blank thread reported as a fork: the engine's open_session does not fork yet (#13031). (#13450) (#13563)
  • Thread gateway: a delivery id that the same device repeats after its 30-day receipt expired, while its row is still in the store, is answered from that row as deduplicated instead of failing with a raw unique-constraint error (the review of #13208). (#13212) (#13279) (#13563)
  • Thread gateway: a session whose file header cannot be read, or names a session kind this build does not know, is never started or reopened unattended. It is refused like a child or worker session instead of being treated as an ordinary interactive one (#13037). (#13279) (#13563)
  • omo remote send in wait mode printed the previous turn's answer and returned before its own turn settled: the follow printed every text_delta it received and settled on the first agent_settled, including the attach's replayed history, which over the relay arrives only after onEvent returns. A send that started or steered a turn now streams its deltas from the aim on (whatever the attach replayed before the aim is dropped) and settles only at its run's agent_settled, so retries and queued follow-ups stream through; a queued send's answer is read from the session's transcript, anchored on the send's own user entry, final when a later message's turn supersedes it or a run settled with it as the tail. A waiting send carries its own clientMessageId, which senpi stamps on the user entry it stores, so the anchor holds when a prompt template or skill expansion rewrote that entry's text and never lands on an older send of the same text; an engine that stores no id falls back to the text match. Carried by the next release train top. (#13272) (#13563)
  • omo remote send in wait mode exited 0 with no output when another device interrupted its turn. It now prints omo remote: the turn on <device>/<session> was interrupted before it finished. and exits with the failure code. (#13272) (#13563)
  • Memory sync settings: when sync cannot read its status, OmO now records WHY. The engine's status path kept one sentence, "Memory sync authority is unavailable.", for every cause, with nothing in the log, so a report of that screen could not be acted on. Each cause now carries a code (no_account, account_aborted, account_not_current, status_read_failed, plus legacy_source where a source answers with no operation-capable account), together with the step that failed, and it is logged once when it starts rather than on every status poll. The device and pending-request reads and the enable and approve operations, which ended in the same sentence, now carry a code too (operation_failed for an unexpected error) and log it with the error; the reads, which the desktop also polls, log once per cause. The message a person sees is unchanged. (#13157) (#13563)
  • Resolved task planner category config live per plan, caching within the plan window to eliminate redundant disk reads and schema validations during child task spawns, and retaining the last known good configuration only when a reload introduces an error (a file that fails to read, parse or validate) the adopted configuration did not already have; warning-level notices such as ignored unknown keys still apply, and revived tasks no longer report a spurious config generation mismatch after a mid-session edit. (#9741, fixes #9725) (#13563)
  • Claude Fable sessions (claude-fable-5, claude-fable-5-1, claude-fable-5-2, on Anthropic, Bedrock and Anthropic-namespaced gateway routes) now get the same assistant-tail repair as Claude Mythos: when the history ends on an assistant turn, the OpenCode messages transform appends the synthetic user turn instead of sending an assistant prefill the model rejects (#13537). (#13537)
  • migrateConfigFile in @oh-my-opencode/utils no longer replaces a config file whose content already equals the migrated output. It used to skip only the backup and still ran the atomic write: a byte-identical replacement that swapped the file's inode and waited on two fsyncs. No current code path calls this function, so the visible effect is in the test suite: the skips backup when file content is identical after migration case no longer waits on disk flushes, which is what let it pass the 20 s limit on a host with stalled storage (#11839). (#13528)
  • bun run test:fast releases the serial quarantine's process group only when that phase finished normally. While a shutdown is in progress the PGID is retained, so the SIGKILL escalation still reaches a descendant that ignored the signal: the orphan case the registry exists to prevent. The child registry gained an explicit release for a finished group and the serial spawner uses it; a test also pins that no ROOT_TEST_SERIAL_QUARANTINE path falls inside the opencode-memory or senpi group scopes, so the split's disjointness is checked rather than assumed. (#13518)
  • All three test:fast groups now pass the canonical per-file budget, read from POSIX_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS in script/root-test-serial-quarantine.ts: the same definition the serial phase and the full command use, with no second copy of the value. Without it only the first file of each group got the preload default and every later file fell back to Bun's built-in budget, so a slow file could fail on the budget rather than on its own behaviour. A test asserts the argv actually spawned for each group name, including Bun's flag order for the --config invocation. (#12031) (#13518)
  • When the temporary directory has a group- or world-writable (or foreign-owned) ancestor, omo now stops with one readable line, omo: trust-tmpdir-unsafe: <dir> is group-writable; run chmod go-w <dir>, or set TMPDIR to a private directory, and start omo again (exit 78), instead of crashing with unsafe trust ancestor and a stack trace (#13503). (#13510)
  • Contributors: the session-manager storage test removes its temporary storage directory after every test block, so the temp-leak guard no longer reports an omo-test-session-manager-* entry. (#13508, fixes #13502) (#13508)
  • bun run test:fast now runs the shared serial quarantine before its three parallel groups, and its root-rest group uses bunfig.win2.parallel.toml, so the local full-suite path no longer runs the 15 quarantined files concurrently, the condition every CI root-test leg forbids. A failing serial phase returns its own exit code and starts no group. Coverage under the new split is pinned at the config-pattern level by a test: the parallel config adds exactly the quarantine paths over its sibling (file counts measured at this head: 4149 = 15 serial + 1435/965/1734 across the three groups, 0 missing, 0 overlap) (#12031). (#12031)

Added

  • thread_create { worktree: { branch?, base? } } creates a git worktree for the new thread, on this device or another one, in OmO's worktrees folder there, and starts the thread in it; every failure (not a repository, branch or folder exists, unknown base, no disk space, no permission, git missing, an older omo on the other device) is a typed code with details.reason and a next action (#13408). A worktree whose thread then fails to open, or whose git worktree add fails part way (including git's timeout), is removed with its branch; what cannot be removed is named in a partial_commit failure (worktree_left_behind). The worktree request another device answers takes only absolute folders and removes only a worktree inside its own worktrees folder on the branch named. (#13450) (#13563)

  • Thread gateway: the store can take in a delivery that another device's service attested for a session on this device that is not running (the intake row of #13037). The row is committed in the same transaction as a same-device delivery, keeps the sender's delivery id, text and display text, is rate-limited per sending device, and is admitted later under the engine's own ledger key, so the engine counts it once even if the same delivery also arrives live. A repeat of a delivery id from the same device is answered with the first answer. A reply to such a delivery continues its chain. Nothing in this release calls the intake yet, so no delivery takes this path. (#13208) (#13279) (#13563)

  • Thread gateway: the store keeps a record of each session a wake asked for or opened (#13037): one row with its state, a lease and a generation that fences every write, at most 4 such sessions past requested per agent directory, and a transient open failure that returns the row to requested with its attempts and the time of the next one (the third deletes it). A wake primitive resolves a durable id to its one session file, refuses child and worker sessions, ensures the host and sends one plain open_session frame (no attended, no permission preset). Nothing calls the wake yet. (#13212) (#13279) (#13563)

  • Thread gateway: the pieces that will let a message from another of your signed-in devices reach a session that is not running on this device are in place but not yet active: the delivery consumer, the carrier that opens such a session in its own working directory and hands it back when its turn is done, and the pending sweep (#13037). Nothing in this release starts them, so a message to a session that is not running is handled as before. (#13220) (#13279) (#13563)

Graphify-Labs/graphify ↗ 2 releases · 2 stable
v0.9.111graphify 0.9.111 Stable2026-11-15T20:17:48Z

Maintenance and security release.

  • Minimum Python is now 3.11 (was 3.10). Python 3.10 reached end of life in October 2026, and the patched releases of our optional and transitive dependencies no longer ship wheels for it. Raising the floor lets the lockfile move to those patched versions. Installs on Python 3.10 keep resolving to 0.9.110, the last 3.10-compatible release; everyone on 3.11 and up is unaffected.
  • Security: with 3.10 dropped, the committed lockfile resolves Pillow 13.0.0, filelock 4.2.4 and opentelemetry-api 1.45.2 for every supported interpreter, clearing the open Dependabot advisories against the older pins. Pillow is only pulled in by the optional svg/all extras, not the core install. This is a dependency and packaging change only: no change to extraction behaviour and the AST cache schema is unchanged.
  • Test: the backtick-substitution runtime tests now skip on bash older than 4.1 (they rely on BASH_XTRACEFD, added in 4.1) instead of misbehaving on the bash 3.2 that macOS ships.

View release →

v0.9.110graphify 0.9.110 Stable2026-11-15T18:11:35Z
  • Fix: python a call through an aliased import (from mod import foo as bar; bar()) is linked from inside a method body and from a decorated function or class def, not just at module level (#5214, thanks @hementhu).
  • Fix: go a type's methods declared in an internal _test.go file (same package foo) fold into the type's package node instead of splitting it and dropping its method-call edges; an external package foo_test stays separate (#5209, thanks @Yi-111-a).
  • Fix: js a name bound in an enclosing scope and captured into a tracked nested closure no longer fabricates a false indirect_call to a same-named corpus function; a genuinely unbound name still resolves (#5217, thanks @Sidreyas).
  • Fix: sql a T-SQL procedure that parses structurally (rather than through ERROR recovery) keeps its INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/SELECT INTO writes, and session temp objects (#t, ##t, @t) are skipped (#5146, thanks @sunhouy).
  • Fix: sql an Oracle CREATE PACKAGE/PACKAGE BODY's member procedures and functions, and their table reads and writes, are recovered instead of yielding only a file node (#5168, thanks @JaynouOliver).
  • Test: llm cover non-fragment array siblings and fragment-less arrays in the single-element-array unwrap (#5192 follow-up, thanks @rohanb123).
  • Fix: extract nested types get owner-qualified node ids, so same-named nested types under different owners (Left.Builder / Right.Builder) no longer collapse into one node, and a qualified call (Outer.Inner.m(), Outer::Inner::m()) resolves through the owner chain; affects C#, Java, Scala, C++ and TypeScript (#5185, thanks @y-src).
  • Fix: query a markdown heading can be read as its whole section body (the new graphify section "<heading>" command and get_section MCP tool), derived from the source file at read time, so the graph and cache are unchanged; paths outside the project are refused (#5166, thanks @nothariharan).
  • Perf: resolution Python parse trees are no longer memoized across resolution passes, cutting peak memory by ~1.6-2 GB on mid-size repos (and ~70% on large ones) in exchange for a small re-parse cost on repos under ~2000 files; graph output is byte-identical (thanks @rohit-jsfreaky). The AST cache schema is bumped to 47; warm caches re-run the affected JS/TS, SQL and nested-type (C#, Java, Scala, C++, TS) extractions.
